description: v2 receptor-anchored CNS liability labels (P33.2) from FDA adverse-reaction tables. basis 'placebo_subtracted' = drug vs placebo arm of a placebo-controlled table; 'absolute_fallback' = no placebo table in any qualifying label, FLAGGED, absolute-incidence rule; 'absent' = no usable label. Built by scripts/v2_liabilities.py; no held-out field is stored, consumers apply pipeline.guards.v2_heldout(inn).
binary_rule: positive (1) iff pooled risk difference >= 5 percentage points AND pooled drug % >= 2 x placebo %. negative (0) otherwise.
fallback_rule: When the selected label has no placebo-controlled table: positive (1) iff a mapped term has drug % >= 10 (CIOMS 'very common') in a non-placebo adverse-reaction table; 0 if the table is present and the mapped terms are absent or below 10; null when only prose is available (recorded as listed_in_prose true/false, no number). Every such row carries basis 'absolute_fallback' and flagged true.

source.population: Table 4. Adverse Reactions Reported by ≥ 2% of INVEGA-Treated Adult Subjects with Schizophrenia in Three Short-Term, Fixed-Dose, Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trials Table includes adverse reactions that were reported in 2% or more of subjects in any of the INVEGA dose groups and which occurred at greater incidence than in the placebo group. Data are pooled from three studies; one study included once-daily INVEGA doses of 3 mg and 9 mg, the second study included 6 mg, 9 mg, and 12 mg, and the third study included 6 mg and 12 mg [see Clinical Studies (14)] . Extrapyramidal symptoms includes the terms dyskinesia, dystonia, extrapyramidal disorder, hypertonia, muscle rigidity, oculogyration, parkinsonism, and tremor. Somnolence includes the terms sedation and somnolence. Tachycardia includes the terms tachycardia, sinus tachycardia, and heart rate increased. Adverse reactions for which the INVEGA incidence was equal to or less than placebo are not listed in the table, but included the following: vomiting.

Extrapyramidal symptoms includes the terms oculogyric crisis, muscle rigidity, musculoskeletal stiffness, nuchal rigidity, torticollis, trismus, bradykinesia, cogwheel rigidity, dyskinesia, dystonia, extrapyramidal disorder, hypertonia, hypokinesia, muscle contractions involuntary, parkinsonian gait, parkinsonism, tremor, and restlessness. other_tables.population: Table 6. Adverse Drug Reactions Reported by ≥ 2% of INVEGA -Treated Adult Subjects with Schizoaffective Disorder in Two Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trials Table includes adverse reactions that were reported in 2% or more of subjects in any of the INVEGA dose groups and which occurred at greater incidence than in the placebo group. Data are pooled from two studies. One study included once-daily INVEGA doses of 6 mg (with the option to reduce to 3 mg) and 12 mg (with the option to reduce to 9 mg). The second study included flexible once-daily doses of 3 to 12 mg. Among the 420 subjects treated with INVEGA, 230 (55%) received INVEGA as monotherapy and 190 (45%) received INVEGA as an adjunct to mood stabilizers and/or antidepressants. Extrapyramidal symptoms includes the terms bradykinesia, drooling, dyskinesia, dystonia, hypertonia, muscle rigidity, muscle twitching, oculogyration, parkinsonian gait, parkinsonism, restlessness, and tremor. Somnolence includes the terms sedation and somnolence. Tachycardia includes the terms tachycardia, sinus tachycardia, and heart rate increased.
